title: Set business continuity requirements from business impact: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: What business harm boundary, recovery time, data-loss tolerance, and dependency evidence define this capability?
focalInsight: BIA establishes priorities; MTD/MAD constrains RTO, RPO constrains loss, and dependencies determine recoverability.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Business Continuity
nodes.definition: Capability to sustain prioritized business outcomes during disruption.
nodes.detail: Capability to sustain prioritized business outcomes during disruption.
nodes.decision: Assess critical function, people, dependencies, workaround.

nodes.label: Business Impact Analysis
nodes.definition: Analysis of impact, critical path, priority, dependency, resources.
nodes.detail: Analysis of impact, critical path, priority, dependency, resources.
nodes.decision: Use impact over time before recovery selection.
nodes.failureExample: Backup chosen before recovery priority known.

nodes.label: Recovery Time Objective
nodes.definition: Target time to restore critical capability.
nodes.detail: Target time to restore critical capability.
nodes.decision: Set below MTD/MAD and test end-to-end.

nodes.label: Recovery Point Objective
nodes.decision: Set from process tolerance and test recovery point.
nodes.failureExample: Fast recovery loses twelve hours against one-hour RPO.

nodes.label: Maximum Tolerable Downtime
nodes.definition: Latest disruption point before unacceptable harm.
nodes.detail: Latest disruption point before unacceptable harm.
nodes.decision: Set business harm boundary and keep RTO shorter.
nodes.failureExample: RTO equals MTD leaving no margin.

nodes.label: External Dependency
nodes.decision: Name owner, SLA, alternate, contact, test.
nodes.failureExample: Replica cannot authenticate because IdP is down.

nodes.label: Recovery Priority
nodes.definition: Restoration order based on impact/critical path.
nodes.detail: Restoration order based on impact/critical path.
nodes.failureExample: Popular dashboard restores before payment intake.

nodes.label: Mtd
nodes.decision: Use interchangeably only after defining organizational harm boundary.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: MTD is harm limit, not restoration target.

nodes.label: RTO
nodes.decision: Use as measured restoration target below MTD.
nodes.failureExample: A test reports uptime without service capability.

altSummary: BIA establishes priorities; MTD/MAD constrains RTO, RPO constrains loss, and dependencies determine recoverability.
textFallback:
business continuity: Capability to sustain prioritized business outcomes during disruption. Decide: Assess critical function, people, dependencies, workaround. Example/failure: Server returns but identity/operator unavailable. Retrieve: Continuity is business capability.
business impact analysis: Analysis of impact, critical path, priority, dependency, resources. Decide: Use impact over time before recovery selection. Example/failure: Backup chosen before recovery priority known. Retrieve: BIA sets requirements.
recovery time objective: Target time to restore critical capability. Decide: Set below MTD/MAD and test end-to-end. Example/failure: Recovery misses business harm window. Retrieve: RTO is recovery target.
recovery point objective: Maximum acceptable data-loss interval. Decide: Set from process tolerance and test recovery point. Example/failure: Fast recovery loses twelve hours against one-hour RPO. Retrieve: RPO measures data loss.
maximum tolerable downtime: Latest disruption point before unacceptable harm. Decide: Set business harm boundary and keep RTO shorter. Example/failure: RTO equals MTD leaving no margin. Retrieve: MTD/MAD constrains RTO.
external dependency: Outside provider/service needed for process. Decide: Name owner, SLA, alternate, contact, test. Example/failure: Replica cannot authenticate because IdP is down. Retrieve: Recovery needs full chain.
recovery priority: Restoration order based on impact/critical path. Decide: Rank outcomes, time sensitivity, dependencies. Example/failure: Popular dashboard restores before payment intake. Retrieve: Priority follows harm.
mtd: Abbreviation for maximum tolerable downtime. Decide: Use interchangeably only after defining organizational harm boundary. Example/failure: Team calls RTO the MTD. Retrieve: MTD is harm limit, not restoration target.
rto: Abbreviation for recovery time objective. Decide: Use as measured restoration target below MTD. Example/failure: A test reports uptime without service capability. Retrieve: RTO requires recoverable critical function.
